reason: The hypothesis relies on premises about entropy stabilization, sluggish diffusion, electronic tuning, and activity/stability enhancements. E4 and E5 directly support entropy stabilization and sluggish diffusion in high-entropy systems, though E5 is for alloy nanoparticles on TiO2, not an HEO support. E1 and E2 show single-atom/d-band tuning and durability in different material classes (LDH, HEA/C), not HEOs. E3 shows activity/stability improvement for CO oxidation on high-entropy spinel oxides, but under dry, lean conditions, not realistic automotive exhaust. The cited evidence is thus partly
premises: High configurational entropy in HEOs stabilizes a homogeneous single-phase structure and suppresses phase separation/sintering.
Sluggish diffusion in high-entropy matrices enhances catalyst durability by suppressing nanoparticle growth.
Single-atom or finely dispersed PGMs in a multimetallic oxide matrix can lower reaction barriers via electronic effects (e.g., d-band center tuning).
Multimetallic oxide systems can promote oxygen vacancy formation and efficient electron transfer, enhancing catalytic activity.
High-entropy oxides demonstrate improved catalytic activity and long-term stability for oxidation reactions compared to simpler oxides.
